title: Pushes & Pulls
description: Welcome to Kinetos Academy! Baron Standstill has drained the Momentum Core and frozen the world's motion. To restart it, you must first master the thing that makes everything move — force.

content.value: Professor Mass ⚖️ gathers you, Anaya 👧 and Arjun 👦. 'Baron Standstill has frozen every push and pull on Earth,' she warns. 'Balls won't roll, doors won't open. Your first mission: understand what a force really is.'
A FORCE is simply a push or a pull. Every time you open a door, kick a ball, or lift a bag, you apply a force. Nothing starts moving, stops, or changes on its own — a force is always behind it.
A force appears only when two objects interact. You push a trolley (you interact with it), a magnet pulls a pin, the Earth pulls a falling apple. No interaction, no force.

PUSH (force away)        PULL (force toward)
🚪  pushing a door        🧲  magnet pulling a pin
⚽  kicking a ball         🎣  reeling in a fishing line
🛒  pushing a trolley      🪢  tug-of-war rope
Net Force: Adding Pushes and Pulls

When two forces act in the SAME direction, they add up. When they act in OPPOSITE directions, we take the difference. In tug-of-war, the team that pulls harder wins because the NET (overall) force is in their direction. If both teams pull equally, the net force is zero and the rope doesn't move — the forces are balanced.
Balanced forces (equal and opposite) cancel out — no change in motion. Unbalanced forces do not cancel — they change how an object moves.
Key Takeaway: A force is a push or a pull that arises from an interaction between two objects. Forces in the same direction add; opposite forces subtract, giving a net force.

quiz.question: A force is best described as…
options: a type of energy stored in objects
quiz.explain: A force is simply a push or a pull that acts on an object.

quiz.question: In a tug-of-war, the rope does NOT move when…
options: both teams pull with equal force (balanced forces)
quiz.explain: Equal and opposite pulls are balanced forces — they cancel out, so the net force is zero and the rope stays still.

quiz.question: Two forces act on a box in the SAME direction. The net force is…
quiz.explain: Forces in the same direction add up to give a larger net force.
